title: sprint-harness configuration
description: The single file that makes the harness portable. Everything project-specific that core/ needs lives here; nothing project-specific lives in core/.

worktree.description: Basename of the directory sprints MUST run from. null disables the check. Set it when the repo has more than one worktree and only one of them is publishable.

map.description: The knowledge base the queue is derived from. Optional: a project can hand-maintain QUEUE.json and skip the map entirely.

requireCommitted.description: Builders run in git worktrees, which materialize only TRACKED files. An uncommitted map is invisible to every builder while you are reading the new one.

checkCmd.description: Optional command that exits non-zero when a derived artifact (an HTML render, an index) is stale.

writeOnlyFrom.description: Worktree basename allowed to run the extractor with --write. File citations resolve against the working tree, so writing the queue from a different worktree can silently produce a different collision graph.

extract.description: How the extractor scrapes file paths out of map prose.

fileExtensions.description: THIS LIST IS THE PARTITIONER. Union-find is correct given its edges, and the edges come from scraping prose — so an extension missing here is a file the collision graph cannot see, and two items editing it get fanned out in parallel. The dangerous case is PARTIAL visibility: an item touching docs/guide.md and src/nav.ts scrapes the .ts, scores `bounded`, and hides the .md collision inside a confident node. Defaults to a typical application stack (ts/tsx/js/go/py/rs/sql/...). A content site, docs repo or design-asset repo MUST set its own list — md, mdx, svg, png, astro, vue. Bare extensions, no dot. The extractor reports any tracked file it found cited whose extension is not listed.

regenerate.description: Commands that REBUILD a generated file from its sources. core/integrate.sh runs them after merging a wave and after the scope gate, then commits any resulting diff before running the merged-tree anchors. A generated file is the paired artifact of EVERY file that feeds it and no node's file list can name it, so no node regenerates it and no anchor checks it — every anchor stays green while the committed artifact silently stops matching the source, and CI is the first thing that notices, after the merge. A pairedArtifacts rule is the wrong fix: most source edits do not move the generated file, so demanding it on every node is noise that gets waived by habit.

why.description: Why this artifact drifts. Write it — the next reader needs to know which source edits move it.

anchors.description: The exit codes this harness trusts. NOT a style preference — an anchor is a command a builder runs and an independent verifier RE-RUNS. A disagreement between the two is the single most valuable signal the system produces.

id.description: Short identifier. Becomes a key in the builder/verifier structured output, so keep it a bare word.

cmd.description: May contain {base}, which resolves to THIS NODE'S base branch — the branch the builder started from, NOT project.mainBranch. Any gate that diffs against a ref needs it: under the stacking rule a batch's base is normally the newest unpushed branch, so judged against main every node inherits every earlier node's failures, and it gets worse the deeper the stack. That both manufactures false ANCHOR DISAGREEMENTs and, worse, stops the gate discriminating — once it is red from inherited failures, a node that genuinely skipped its own artifact cannot fail louder. An unknown placeholder throws before any agent spawns. A CACHING RUNNER NEEDS ITS CACHE OFF HERE: an anchor is a command a verifier RE-RUNS, and a result cache keyed on inputs and shared across worktrees (go test, jest, pytest plugins) can hand the verifier a pass produced by the builder's tree or by a sibling verifier. Both sides then report the same exit code from the same cache entry, so the claimed-vs-observed comparison cannot fail and the system's most valuable signal is silently dead. Pass the runner's no-cache flag (`go test -count=1`, `jest --no-cache`) in `cmd`.

always.description: false makes this anchor CONDITIONAL, which gives it a third state besides pass and fail. Both the builder and the verifier are told to report null when it did not apply, and the reduce skips any comparison where either side is null. A null on an always:true anchor is a required check nobody ran and is warned about.

whenTouches.description: Run this anchor only when the diff touches one of these paths/prefixes. Keeps a slow anchor off nodes that cannot have broken it.

serialize.description: Hold a host-wide lock while this anchor runs, so only one copy executes on the box at a time. Set it on any anchor that sizes its own worker pool to the core count -- a test runner, typically. A wave starts an anchor up to 2N times at once (one builder plus one anchors verifier per node), which oversubscribes the machine N-fold and turns timeouts into red exit codes that look like code failures. Measured: 8 concurrent runs of a suite that is green alone came back 8/8 red, 200 failures, every one a timeout and not one an assertion. Costs wall-clock; buys a number the builder and the verifier can both stand behind. See docs/SCARS.md #35.

setup.description: Commands every builder and verifier runs BEFORE the anchors, in a fresh worktree.

why.description: Shown verbatim in the agent contracts. Say what breaks if the agent improvises a shortcut — agents skip steps whose cost they cannot see.

lanes.description: Categories of work that CANNOT be parallelised against each other, regardless of which files they touch. The canonical case is numbered forward-only migrations: two agents cannot both mint the next number, and no merge can resolve it.

itemFlag.description: Boolean field on a queue item. Every selected item with this flag truthy is unioned into one serial node.

pairedArtifacts.description: Mechanical 'if you changed X you must also change Y' gates, with an auditable waiver. This exists because the same rule as PROSE in an agent contract produced three test files across fifty-one components.

pairPath.description: Template for the required counterpart. {name} = source basename without extension. e.g. "web/components/__tests__/{name}.test.tsx"

waiverTrailer.description: Commit-message trailer that waives the rule for ONE named source file. Blanket waivers are unsupported on purpose — an exemption must be greppable and arguable.

help.description: Printed on failure. Point at the pattern to copy.

lenses.description: One verifier per lens per node, each with a context that has never seen the builder's. Distinct QUESTIONS, not redundant reviewers — which is why ONE reject fails a node rather than being outvoted.

requireAllLenses.description: A node is accepted only when every lens actually returned. A lens that crashed leaves the node UNVERIFIED, which is not the same outcome as rejected.

model.description: OPTIONAL, and normally unset. Pins every verifier to one model instead of inheriting the main loop. The prompts are unchanged either way, so the only variable is the model -- which is what makes a second opinion measurable rather than anecdotal. A slug here rots faster than anything else in this file; leave it out unless you are deliberately running a comparison, and never let it silently become the default.

confirmAccepted.description: OPTIONAL, DEFAULT OFF, and it DOUBLES the verifier spend. Re-verifies every node the FIRST pass accepted, with fresh contexts and the same lenses, and a reject in either pass fails the node. It buys detection, not precision. Measured over four arms on a rig of planted defects: one run caught 11 of 12, while every pairwise union of two runs caught 12 of 12 -- and the union costs nothing because rejects were precise, 0 false rejects across 12 control-node judgements. A lens that crashes in the CONFIRM pass leaves the node accepted with a warning: the first pass already met the bar, and a flaky second pass must not fail good work.

denyPushReason.description: Shown to the agent on denial. State what the real gate is, so the agent stops instead of hunting for another route.

stackBranches.description: When true, preflight refuses to call the main branch a valid base while ANY local branch is ahead of the remote. Branching from main there silently drops every unpushed commit from your base.

excludeFromStacking.description: Branches that are permanently ahead of the remote by design (a demo branch, a never-pushed integration branch) and are therefore not stacking bases.

marker.description: String that must appear in .git/hooks/pre-push for preflight to consider the guard installed.
